newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan two-month NCD average yield at 7.254 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan two-month NCD average yield at 7.254 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank issued T$13 billion in two-month negotiable certificates of deposit on Thursday at an average yield of 7.254 percent, a central bank official said.
The range of the bids was between 6.98 and 7.40 percent.
The issue coincides with a renewed bull run in Taiwan's stock market, where the index has pushed to a series of seven-year highs in recent weeks.
Thursday was no exception, with the index surging to another seven-year high close at 9,429.74.
Taiwan's overnight and short-term money rates soared into double digits in late June as investors diverted holdings into the share market.
Some investors had also liquidated their foreign exchange holdings into Taiwan dollars, bolstering the local currency and halting what had been a slow, steady devaluation.
The currency's value again has been eroding in recent days, though it rebounded sharply on Thursday to close at T$27.855 to the U.S. dollar against Wednesday's T$27.926 finish.

The central bank repeatedly issued NCDs when the index was hottest in March and April, a move widely seen as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say was fuelling the dramatic rally.
The central bank has confirmed that it was responding to the liquidity sitution but denied that it was acting directly in response to the stock market bull run.
